DEPARTMENT OF
Inland Fisheries and Game
MAYNARD F. MARSH, COMMISSIONER
AUGUSTA, MAINE 04330
April 12, 1972
Mr. Yates M. Barber, Jr.
Acting Chief
Office of Environmental Quality
U. S. Department of the Interior
Fish and Wildlife Service
Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife
Washington, D. C. 20240
Dear Sir:
Pursuant to your request relative to Section 102 (2)(C) of the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969, we submit the following comments relative to H.R. 1311, Proposed Endangered Species Act of 1972.
The Department of Inland Fisheries and Game has grave reservations with respect to this change in the law. It is our feeling that the States should retain a strong role in the management of rare and endangered species within its jurisdiction, and that the Secretary of Interior should allow the States to retain their historic roles in the management of fish, wildlife and marine resources.
We cite, as a case in point, the joint Federal-State Management Program of the Atlantic sea-run salmon, wherein the State of Maine has mounted and is carrying out an intensive restoration program.
Yours very truly,
Maynard F. Marsh
Commissioner
